newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Coega port plan wins government blessing.
newsitem.headline: S.African Coega port plan wins government blessing.

text.p: Plans for a new port and industrial development zone in South Africa's depressed Eastern Cape province took a major step forward on Tuesday after winning the blessing of a ministerial committee.
The Department of Trade and Industry said the project at Coega near Port Elizabeth had been given support in principle and officials would prepare details to put to cabinet.
Backers say the planned bulk harbour and adjacent industrial zone will attract major industry, creating thousands of jobs in an area suffering unemployment rates of 40-50 percent.
"It's a giant leap forward for the Coega project," Kevin Wakeford, chief executive of the Port Elizabeth Chamber of Commerce, told Reuters.
"It's now really a question of getting down to the details, including the financial mechanism and the statutory requirements."
Feasibility studies have recommended that construction start early in 1998, leading to completion of the port and phase one of the industrial zone by 2001.
The ambitious scheme requires both the backing of the government, which will have to stump up cash to provide basic infrastructure, and the commitment of a handful of risk-taking companies.
Wakeford believes the rationale for Coega is the shift in the South African economy from import substitution to export-driven manufacturing, leading to a shift in industry to the coast.

Catalyst for the scheme is a planned 220,000-tonne-a-year zinc refinery by Gencor Ltd. The company has identified Coega as its preferred site but the zinc plant has yet to win the green light from the Gencor board.
Other plans for the industrial zone include a fertiliser plant proposed by AECI Ltd subsidiary Kynoch and a cement factory by Pretoria Portland Cement Ltd.

Several other South African companies have expressed interest in setting up on the industrial area behind the planned port. Coega's backers also hope foreign businesses will be attracted to the region.
The Department of Trade and Industry said cabinet would process the matter soon, after which more detailed announcements would be made.
Reacting to concerns from environmentalists, the department added that every step would be taken to ensure the project was environmentally sustainable.
